question: Can the bore-to-track offset be learned from the section profile, and does it then expose the adjacent-track lock failure?
features: 64-bin centred lateral profile at the probed range, 64-bin mean near-field profile (10 and 15 m), plus range, analytic near-field offset, symmetry score, section width, near width, near symmetry score, width difference, bore axis (136 total)
protocol: Leave-one-recording-out. Excursion frames (|centre| > 1 m at the 30 m probe) are excluded from training because their target is the quantity that is wrong; predicting on them is therefore a test on an unseen regime. scikit-learn is not a declared project dependency and no training code is added to the package.
conclusion: The section profile carries the offset: pooled median error falls to 0.053 m against 0.207 m for the analytic constant and 0.166 m for claiming the track runs down the sensor axis, and the model beats that trivial claim by 7.5x on the one recording with a real mounting yaw, so it is not reproducing a zero. Used as a check on frames it never trained on, the predicted centre disagrees with the rails by 1.70 m against 0.05 m on clean frames, catching 90 percent of excursion rows at 2.5 percent false on clean rows. Limits: the excursion label is our own rail-based criterion rather than ground truth, six recordings in two mounting configurations cannot establish transfer to another tunnel, and this detects the failure without yet correcting it.
